acceptanceCriteria: Given a valid promo object with an applicable trip scope and a date range, when `promoAppliesToLineItem` is called with a return-trip line item whose `date.dateTo` falls within the promo's validity window, then it MUST return `true`, ensuring the return trip is not excluded from promo discount calculation.

The email confirmation rendering logic for Mozio MUST include the promo code discount amount for both outbound and return trip line items when a promo code is applied to a round-trip order; the total discount displayed MUST equal the sum of outbound and return promo discounts.
Given `null` or `undefined` as the `promo` argument, when `promoAppliesToLineItem` is called, then it MUST return `false` (not any truthy value).

Given a valid promo object with a defined validity window, when `promoAppliesToLineItem` is called with a return-trip line item whose `date.dateTo` falls OUTSIDE the promo's validity window, then it MUST return `false`.
Given a promo object whose trip scope does not include the line item's trip type, when `promoAppliesToLineItem` is called with that line item, then it MUST return `false`.
Given a line item that has no `date` property or a `date` property with no `dateTo` field, when `promoAppliesToLineItem` is called with a valid promo, then it MUST return `false`.
Given a promo object that is missing validity date fields (e.g., `startDate`/`endDate` or equivalent), when `promoAppliesToLineItem` is called with any line item, then it MUST return `false`.

The test suite for `src/services/mozio/email-promo-discount.ts` MUST include a test case that passes a valid promo object and a return-trip line item to `promoAppliesToLineItem` and asserts a `true` return value.

The test suite for `src/services/mozio/email-promo-discount.ts` MUST include a test case that passes `null` or `undefined` as the `promo` argument to `promoAppliesToLineItem` and asserts a `false` return value.

The test suite MUST include an integration or template-level test verifying that when a round-trip Mozio order with an applied promo code is rendered into the email confirmation, the promo discount amount appears for both the outbound and return trip sections.

Given a one-way trip order with an applied promo code, when the email confirmation is rendered, then the promo discount amount MUST still be displayed correctly on the single trip line item (regression guard).

Given a round-trip order where the promo code applies to only the outbound leg, when the email confirmation is rendered, then the discount MUST appear only on the outbound line item and MUST NOT appear on the return line item.

notes: Modified AC3 (was openspec AC3): removed the `node -e` verification command which violated the WHAT-NOT-HOW rule by prescribing a specific runtime verification approach; replaced with Given/When/Then behaviour statement. Modified AC5→AC9 (was openspec AC5): removed the `grep` verification command for the same reason; the test-existence criterion is retained as an observable outcome (test suite contains the case). Added AC4: return-trip line item outside validity window must return false — the positive case was covered but the negative boundary was missing. Added AC5: promo scope mismatch must return false — critical edge case for trip-type filtering. Added AC6: missing date/dateTo on line item must return false — guards against undefined-property access errors. Added AC7: promo missing validity dates must return false — another null-safety edge case. Added AC11: one-way trip regression guard — ensures the fix doesn't break the existing one-way promo display path. Added AC12: partial-scope round-trip — ensures the system correctly handles promos that apply to only one leg, preventing over-application of discounts.
